newsitem.title: USA: NYC council sees state bonus if welfare rolls fall.
newsitem.headline: NYC council sees state bonus if welfare rolls fall.

text.p: New York City Council said Wednesday that the amount of surplus for the state under the new federal welfare law could hit $458 million in fiscal year 1997 if welfare caseloads fall three percent a year.

The data, which were released in the council's report on the fiscal effect of welfare reform, also showed that the surplus for the Empire State would rise steadily to $727 million in 2002, assuming welfare rolls fell three percent a year.
A spokesman for the City Council said the city budget projects its welfare cases will have fallen 15 percent from the 1995 fiscal year to the end of the 1998 fiscal year.
The head of the council's finance committee, Herbert Berman, stressed that any extra funds should be reinvested in healthcare, education, and in helping people who now collect welfare find jobs.

"If we don't use this as an opportunity to help people build the skills they need to become independent, when the five-year time limit is up New York City and the state will have to share the full cost of supporting people who can't work," said Berman in prepared remarks.
The new federal welfare rules impose a five-year time limit on certain types of benefits.
